what_its_for: Pramlintide is used along with insulin to help control blood sugar levels in adults with Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes. It works by slowing down how fast food leaves your stomach, reducing sugar released by your liver after meals, and helping you feel full sooner so you eat less.
how_to_take: Pramlintide is given as a shot (injection) under the skin (subcutaneously). Inject it into your stomach area (abdomen) or thigh — never into your arm. Always inject pramlintide as a SEPARATE shot from your insulin — do NOT mix them together in the same syringe. Use a different spot each time to avoid skin irritation. Rotate your injection sites. Give the shot right before each major meal (a meal with at least 250 calories or 30 grams of carbohydrates).
dosing: For Type 2 Diabetes: Start with 60 micrograms (mcg) before each major meal. Your doctor may increase your dose to 120 mcg per meal if you are tolerating it well after 3 to 7 days. For Type 1 Diabetes: Start with 15 mcg before each major meal. Your doctor will slowly increase your dose (by 15 mcg at a time) up to 30 or 60 mcg per meal as tolerated. IMPORTANT: When you start pramlintide, your mealtime insulin dose will need to be reduced — usually by 50%. Your doctor will guide you on this. Always follow your doctor's specific dosing instructions.
missed_dose: If you forget to take your pramlintide dose before a meal, skip that missed dose and wait until your next scheduled meal to take your next dose. Do NOT take extra pramlintide to make up for a missed dose. Never inject pramlintide after you have already eaten.
storage: Unopened (unused) pens or vials: Store in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze. Throw away if it has been frozen. Opened (in-use) pens or vials: May be kept in the refrigerator OR at room temperature (below 77°F / 25°C) for up to 28 days. Throw away after 28 days, even if there is medicine left. Keep away from direct heat and light. Keep out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how pramlintide affects your blood sugar — it can cause low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), especially when combined with insulin. Avoid skipping meals after taking pramlintide, as this raises your risk of low blood sugar. Avoid alcohol, as it can make low blood sugar worse and harder to recognize. Do not mix pramlintide in the same syringe as insulin. Avoid taking pramlintide if you have slow stomach emptying (gastroparesis), as it may worsen this condition. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about all your other medications, because pramlintide can slow the absorption of pills taken by mouth — if you need a medication to work quickly (like pain relievers), take it at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after your pramlintide shot.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: Signs of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) — shakiness, dizziness, sweating, confusion, fast heartbeat, hunger, or fainting. Signs of severe allergic reaction — rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing. Nausea or vomiting that is severe or does not get better. Blood sugar levels that are consistently too high or too low. Redness, swelling, or hard lumps at your injection site that do not go away. Any new or unusual symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Pramlintide starts working within about 20 minutes of injection and its effects last for approximately 3 hours, covering the rise in blood sugar that happens after a meal. You may notice improvements in your after-meal blood sugar levels relatively quickly, but it may take several weeks of consistent use — along with proper diet, exercise, and insulin therapy — to see the full benefit in your overall blood sugar control (A1C levels).
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: It is not known if pramlintide is safe during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Older Adults (65+): Use with extra caution, as older adults may have a higher risk of falls or injury from low blood sugar. Blood sugar should be monitored closely. Children and Teenagers: Pramlintide is not approved for use in patients under 18 years of age. Kidney or Liver Problems: Pramlintide is generally safe in patients with mild to moderate kidney disease, but your doctor should be aware of your kidney function. Always tell your healthcare team about all your medical conditions before starting this medication.
